title: Return requests
description: Handle returns, exchanges and refund requests.

help.title: About Return requests
help.overview: A return request asks to send goods back, swap them, or get money back for a product order. Its type is return, exchange, or refund, and its status walks pending → approved or rejected → received → completed. Customers raise them from their account; staff can also create them here.

sections.title: What a request contains
sections.body: A request always points at one order and specific lines of it.
items: Each line is an order item, a quantity, and a reason. Only shipped quantities can be claimed, and units already claimed by another open request are not available again.
The refund amount is optional and can never exceed the value of the claimed lines.
A till sale cannot be returned here; it is refunded on the till.
Once requested, the lines are fixed. The customer note and admin note stay on the request.
Staff with access to returns are notified when a new request is saved.

sections.title: Decide: approve or reject
sections.body: Both are only for a pending request. Both record who decided and when, and the customer is told.
items: Approve can set or correct the refund amount, still capped at the value of the claimed lines, and can add an admin note.
Reject closes the request with an optional reason. It moves no stock and no money.

sections.title: Receive: goods come back
sections.body: Receive is only for an approved request.
items: For a return or an exchange, the claimed units go back on hand in the warehouse each line shipped from, and a return movement is written for each. A bundle comes back as its components.
A line whose sale never took stock (an untracked product) or whose stock row is gone is noted on the order timeline instead of restocked.
A refund-only request has nothing to receive; receiving it only advances the status.

sections.title: Complete: money goes back
sections.body: Complete is only after the request has been received.
items: For a return or a refund with a refund amount, completing runs the order's refund for that amount, through the gateway for card payments. This also needs permission to write the order's payment status.
An exchange pays nothing back; the replacement is handled as new fulfilment work.
If the refund covers everything left on the order, the order's full-refund rules apply too.

sections.title: Related pages
items: The order shows the refund, the restocking notes, and the timeline.
Stock movements show the return entries with this request as their reference.
Deleting a request is a soft delete and it can be restored.
